title: U.S. House · New Hampshire's 1st District
area: Eastern New Hampshire, including Manchester, Portsmouth and Rochester.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Rep. Chris Pappas (D) did not seek re-election here and is instead the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. Stefany Shaheen, daughter of retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.2% of the vote over Maura Sullivan (34.9%) and Carleigh Beriont (22.0%).

candidates.name: Stefany Shaheen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.2% of the vote in a nine-candidate field.
candidates.currentRole: Former Portsmouth, NH City Councilor and Chair of the Portsmouth Police Commission

summary.text: Stefany Shaheen is the Democratic nominee for New Hampshire's open 1st Congressional District and the daughter of retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen. According to her campaign website, she is a co-founder of the health company Good Measures, the author of a best-selling book about her family's experience with type 1 diabetes, and a former Portsmouth city councilor who chaired the Portsmouth Police Commission. She is running on health care and affordability.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she lives in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, where she and her husband, Craig, raised their family; she is the mother of four children. She also says she grew up in New Hampshire and built a small business there.

According to her campaign website, she is a graduate of Fairfield University, where she was a Division 1 scholarship athlete, and an alumna of MIT's Sloan School of Management and Harvard's Kennedy School of Government.

Says she has spent more than 15 years advocating for medical research on chronic disease, motivated by her eldest daughter's type 1 diabetes diagnosis at age eight, and has helped raise millions of dollars for research.

Co-founded Good Measures, a company that connects people with chronic conditions to clinical and decision-making support; her campaign website says it was awarded patents in the U.S. and ten other countries. Citizens Count lists her as its co-founder and president.

Author of Elle & Coach, which her campaign website describes as a New York Times best-selling book about her family's experience with type 1 diabetes. Her website also says she served on the President's Council on Sports, Fitness and Nutrition.
Elected to the Portsmouth City Council; Citizens Count lists her service as 2014 to 2016. Her campaign website cites work on a downtown parking shortage and PFAS testing of the local water supply.

Chaired the Portsmouth Police Commission (2019 to 2024, per Citizens Count). Her campaign website says she was also appointed by Gov. John Lynch to chair the state's Commission on the Status of Women.
Currently part of a bio-tech initiative in Manchester's millyard focused on regenerative medicine, according to her campaign website.
Won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat; Rep. Chris Pappas is running for U.S. Senate rather than re-election.

priorities.text: Health care: says corporate monopolies and Wall Street investors have driven up health care costs, and says she supports Medicare for All and a public option while pursuing near-term steps such as breaking up health care monopolies and lowering prescription drug prices.

Affordability: opposes tariffs imposed by the Trump administration, saying they have raised costs for small businesses and consumers, and calls for refunding revenue collected from tariffs the Supreme Court found illegal.

Housing: says investor purchases of homes and tax breaks for hedge funds and private equity firms are driving up housing costs, and calls for ending those tax breaks and expanding support for first-time homebuyers.

positions.summary: Says she supports Medicare for All and a public option, and wants to break up health care corporate monopolies and let Medicare negotiate lower drug prices.
Calls for rolling back tariffs she describes as illegal and refunding the money they cost small businesses.
Calls for cutting red tape that prevents construction of new affordable housing and investing in the skilled trades to build homes faster.
Calls for overhauling ICE, including body cameras, a ban on masks, ending warrantless searches, and ending raids in schools, churches and hospitals.

candidates.name: Anthony DiLorenzo

summary.text: Anthony DiLorenzo is the Republican nominee for New Hampshire's open 1st Congressional District and a first-time candidate for public office. He is the founder of Key Auto Group, a chain of car dealerships and collision centers, and a real estate developer based in Portsmouth. He is running as a political outsider with a focus on energy costs and affordability, and has the endorsement of President Donald Trump.

background.text: Says he was raised in a working-class family and got his first job delivering newspapers at age eight; he has lived in New Hampshire for 43 years, according to an interview in The Dartmouth.
Says he attended the University of New Hampshire, dropped out, and started his own business with $7,000.

Founder of Key Auto Group, which The Dartmouth reports operates 21 car dealerships and 12 collision centers in nine states; New Hampshire Public Radio describes it as employing more than 1,000 people.

Also a real estate developer who has been involved in hotel development, owns Planet Fitness franchises, and was the winning bidder for redevelopment of the McIntyre building in downtown Portsmouth, where he lives.
Gave $4 million to the University of New Hampshire in 2023, according to New Hampshire Public Radio.
Is a first-time candidate who has not previously held public office. President Donald Trump endorsed him in July 2026.
Won the September 8, 2026 Republican primary, defeating Hollie Noveletsky, Brian Cole, Melissa Bailey and Lindsey Anderson.

candidates.researchNotes: DiLorenzo has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, and his campaign website was not reachable in the time available; only a brief Ballotpedia biography was found.
